title: Grok 4
hook: xAI's Grok 4 leaned hard on reinforcement learning and native tool use, topping several reasoning benchmarks at its July 2025 launch.
key_points: xAI's frontier model, released July 2025, trained with large-scale reinforcement learning.
Built-in tool use and a version tuned for agentic, multi-step tasks.
Claimed leading scores on hard reasoning benchmarks at launch.
Integrated with X and offered via the xAI API and a premium subscription.
content_html: xAI released Grok 4 in July 2025, positioning it as a frontier reasoning model and the centerpiece of its push to compete with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. The release emphasized heavy reinforcement-learning post-training and native tool use, with the company claiming top scores on several demanding reasoning evaluations.
extra_html:
What's new

Grok 4 scaled up the reinforcement-learning stage that had become central to reasoning models, training the model to work through problems and call tools as part of its thinking. xAI also offered a variant aimed at long-horizon agentic tasks. The model is tightly integrated with the X platform and is available through the xAI API and a premium subscription tier.

Why it matters

Grok 4 marked xAI's arrival as a serious frontier contender within a couple of years of founding, underscoring how quickly a well-resourced lab can reach the frontier given enough compute and the now-standard RL-on-reasoning recipe. Its launch benchmarks were strong, though as always the durable test is real-world use rather than leaderboard numbers.

related.title: GPT-5
related.hook: GPT-5 folds OpenAI's two lines into one: a router decides on the fly whether a prompt needs a fast answer or deep step-by-step reasoning, so you stop picking models.

related.title: OpenAI o3: Reasoning that Uses Tools
related.hook: o3 is the first reasoning model that can agentically reach for every ChatGPT tool mid-thought - web search, Python on your files, image input, image generation - and combine them to solve a problem.

related.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
related.hook: DeepSeek shows strong reasoning can emerge from RL on verifiable rewards with minimal supervised data - and those reasoning traces can be distilled into smaller models.
